quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When using a sidecar to transport a load, you should:

options.text: Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load unsecured in the seat.
Secure the load near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the sidecar nose from tipping up during sharp left turns.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for at least one hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: Riding alongside another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
Makes it easier for other vehicles to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcyclist. It limits both of your escape routes if you encounter a hazard.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other traffic is at intersections. Be extra alert at intersections where another vehicle may cross your path.

questions.question: To increase your chances of being seen at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on is the most important thing you can do to help others see you at an intersection. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This allows more experienced riders at the back to watch them.

questions.question: Braking in a turn is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straightaway.
More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
Done safely by using the front brake only.
Done safely by using the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is more difficult than braking on a straightaway. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must know the correct technique and be very careful.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the driver will yield to you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
Means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact with another driver means they will yield the right-of-way to you. Never take this as a guarantee.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Does not mean that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver sees you. A driver can look directly at you and still not actually notice you.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Your entire face, not just your eyes.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good replacement for either one.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
Move between different parts of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing car increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, rain, and cold.
Taking artificial stimulants like pills or energy drinks.
Limiting how far you ride in one day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants like pills or energy drinks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from weather. Never use artificial stimulants because they are dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: At what point does alcohol impair your riding ability?
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment begins well before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing your motorcycle?

options.text: Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog. Once you are close to it, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: Which of the following gives a rider the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield and eyeglasses do not provide the same protection.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chance of a crash during the day when most crashes happen?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible by wearing bright-colored clothing, even during the day.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chance of an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you very closely.
Focus only on your controls and not the road ahead.
Let other drivers know your intentions with signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know your intentions with signals.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs showing rules like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles happen because of improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake?

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only under slippery conditions.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when you use it correctly.

questions.question: What is important about rain suits for motorcycles?

options.text: Are not needed since motorcycles shouldn't be operated in the rain.

questions.explanation: Good rain suits made for motorcycles will not tear or balloon out when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close together while maintaining safe space?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in broad daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials helps other drivers see you at all times.
